rows: Glass frame edge to side wall

steps: Unpack & check the packet

Unbolt the fireplace from its pallet and bend up the shipping clips. Check the manual packet: glass latch tool, remote with 3 AAA batteries, backup battery holder with 4 AA, backup power harness and the owner's manual. All of it stays with the homeowner.

Glass latch tool#HA-77-00256
Remote transmitter#HA-110-00105 · 3-AAA #65-06-01270
Backup battery holder#05-02-00345 · 4 AA #65-06-01147
Backup power harness#10-03-00128

Contact Mendota Technical Service if any parts are missing. The log set, firebox liner and decorative front are not included; each is selected and bought separately.

Net weight 325 lbs; team lift recommended. The four lifting handles (one on each side, two on the rear wall) are only for lifting and shifting the unit short distances, not for carrying it: remove the screw on each handle's upper section and pull it outward.
LP conversion (if burning propane)
Kit #HA-88-00080: a motorized LP pressure regulator plus #55 (front) and 1/16" (rear) burner orifices, and the pilot set to LP. Best done before the unit goes into its framed cavity.

The unit ships for natural gas. The kit must be installed by a qualified service agency. Shut off the gas supply, then turn off the electrical supply, before starting.

  1. Remove the 4 screws (¼" hex) holding the two burner tubes, slide the tubes right and lift them out, then lift out the burner airbox with the front grate attached.
  2. Turn off gas at the appliance service valve if the line is connected; remove the left-side valve access cover (eight ¼" hex screws).
  3. Change the orifice spuds with a ½" deep-well socket while holding the back-side fitting with an open-end wrench: rear #65-14-00116 (1/16" drill), front #65-14-00055 (#55 drill).
  4. Pilot (right side of the firebox, where the burner ends meet): hold the base with large vice grips, loosen the hood ¼ turn with a 7/16" open-end wrench (don't remove it), push the NG/LP clip in until "NAT" isn't visible, then retighten.
  5. Regulator: with a Torx T20 (supplied) or slotted screwdriver, remove and discard the two mounting screws, the regulator tower and the spring/diaphragm assembly; check the rubber gasket is in place; fit the stepper-motor regulator with the supplied M4 x 0.7 screws at 25 lb-in ± 5; put the identification label on the valve body.
  6. Refit the valve cover, burner airbox and burners, with the burner tube curves parallel to the airbox air slots. Attach the kit's labels to the back of the listing-label plate.

Then check inlet and outlet pressures, install the logs and glass door, and light with the remote. The burner must light immediately without lifting; pilot flames at least 1" long and overlapping the propagation ports on both burners.

Stripped or damaged valve threads mean replacing the valve. Correct operation can't be guaranteed if the kit or valve has been dropped or hit hard.
Frame, hearth & set the unit

Frame to the minimums (51" enclosure width, 45" finished framing width, 48 1/2" high, 22-1/2" deep), plan the hearth pad and finishing guides, then set the unit on wood, masonry or metal, level and plumb it, and secure it to the framing studs.

• Plan the finishing guides before any hearth pad or wall finish goes on. The standard guide suits inside-finish fronts; doors use the guides in the door kit; Grace, Willowbrook and Mission fronts need a Flush Mount or a Recessed Mount guide kit. All guides protrude 1" and stay permanently in place.
  • Materials in non-combustible areas must be non-combustible per NFPA 220 or pass ASTM E 136. Paper-faced gypsum board (including Type X) and WonderBoard are not approved there. At least 1" of finish depth over the fireplace (the guides' depth) is recommended.
  • Before finishing, remove any front, screen or door and mask the glass frame.
  • Open the glass door and check the accent light: bulb and lens ship installed (G9 Xenon 25W bulb #10-11-00020). Handle the bulb only with its foam wrap or clean gloves, and don't over-tighten the four 10-24 lens nuts.
  • Mobile home (USA): bolt the unit to the floor and ground it.
Note: p. 29 says wall finish deeper than 2 ½" requires the Recessed Mount guide kit, and also that the Flush Mount kit takes finish material less than 3" thick, including backing materials.
Install the vent system

5" x 8" coaxial rigid pipe, every joint twist-locked, no silicone; 12" minimum vertical off the starter collar. Keep 1" to combustibles at the sides and bottom and 3" above horizontal runs, use a wall thimble through any combustible wall, and set the cap right-side-up and sealed.

• Measure the length needed; pre-assembling the run helps locate the penetrations.
  • Horizontal termination: with the minimum 12" vertical and one 90°, the elbow centerline is 57 1/2" above floor level (add ¼" rise per foot of horizontal run). Frame 10-3/4" x 10-3/4" for the mandatory wall thimble (a 9-inch diameter hole is acceptable in non-combustible walls). Combustible wall thickness 4" to 8" maximum. The pipe ends flush with the exterior wall; screw the cap to the wall and caulk it, never recessed into the siding.
  • Vinyl, wood or other combustible siding: use heat shield #AA-11-00458 (or an equivalent).
  • Ceilings: frame 10 ½" x 10 ½" for the mandatory ceiling fire stop; add an attic insulation shield; enclose the vent through occupied spaces above the first floor.
  • Roof: cut 10" x 10", seal the flashing with roofing over its top edge, then storm collar and cap. Roof surface to top of cap ("H"): flat to 6/12 and 7/12 to 9/12, 2 ft; 10/12 to 12/12, 4 ft; 13/12 to 16/12, 6 ft; 17/12 to 21/12, 8 ft.
  • Support horizontal runs and vertical runs every 3 ft.
  • Termination clearances, from the cap center: 12" above grade, deck or porch (24" for vinyl surfaces); 12" to a window or door that opens; 18" below a ventilated or unventilated soffit (24" vinyl); 7" to an outside corner; 12" to an inside corner (24" vinyl); not above a meter/regulator within 3 feet horizontally; 3 feet to a service regulator vent; 12" to a non-mechanical air inlet; 6 feet to a mechanical air inlet; 7 feet above a public paved walk or driveway; 12" under a veranda, porch or deck; 24" horizontal to any surface for vertical caps.
  • Two direct vent caps side by side: 18" minimum between vertical centerlines. Vertical caps close together need an 18-gauge or heavier galvanized barrier 6" taller and 3" wider than the caps.
Note: pp. 60 and 62 say to frame 10 ½" x 10 ½" for the ceiling fire stop; p. 62 also says fire stops at the second floor and above are framed to 10" x 10" inside dimensions.
Gas supply & leak test

1/2" N.P.T. female inlet, with the supply piping entering on the left side. Size the line from the supply regulator to the factory shutoff valve with the table on p. 43. CSST needs brass-to-brass fittings, a drip leg is recommended, never plastic pipe. Leak-test every field and factory joint with soap solution or a gas sniffer.

The factory-installed manual shutoff valve sits in the left-side convection chamber; turn it with the glass latch tool (down 90° closes, up 90° opens). Supply a ½" NPT male fitting for the ½" female inlet. Where local code requires one, add an external keyed wall- or floor-mounted manual shutoff valve. Some areas allow copper tubing or galvanized pipe; check local codes.

A gas line that is too small can lead to improper burner ignition. Supply pressure: NG 7" W.C. (5.0" min., 11" max.); LP 11" W.C. (11" min., 13" max.).

Supply-piping pressure tests: above 1/2 psi (3.5 kPa), disconnect the appliance and its main gas valve; at 1/2 psi or less, isolate it by closing its shutoff valve.
Verify orifices & input rate

Check the orifice size stamped on each orifice body (NG #37 rear / #44 front up to 2000 ft; LP 1/16" rear / #55 front), set manifold pressure (NG 3.5" WC ± 1/8", LP 10.0" WC ± 1/8") and clock the gas meter over 30 minutes.

1. Turn off all other gas appliances and their pilots; read the gas meter.
  2. Run the fireplace 30 minutes at maximum flame, turn off the burner and pilot, and read the meter again.
  3. Final minus initial reading = therms used. Multiply by 100,000, then by 2.
  4. The result must be at least 45,500 Btu below 2000 feet, or at least 44,500 Btu above 2000 feet.

High altitude: ask the gas supplier first; orifices may not need changing if the supply is already adjusted. When de-rating, fill in the High-Altitude De-Rating Label (owner's manual packet) and attach it to the back of the listing-label plate in the air gap below the glass frame. Above 7,500 ft, contact Mendota Technical Service.

Note: for the high-altitude orifices (2000–4500 ft), p. 15 gives rear #37 NG and front #56 LP; p. 46 gives rear #38 NG with front #55 LP ("for all elevations").
Electrical & DC backup inlet

Run constant-hot 120 VAC (no switch) to the junction box on the left side, join the wires color to color with the supplied wire nuts, and plug in the house-power lead. Mount the supplied DC backup inlet box up to 5 feet to the left, 18" maximum to the box center.
Liner, logs & glass door

Install the firebox liner kit and one log set (Norway Spruce, White Oak, Birch or Premium Fiber Oak) with its coals and inswool media, each per its own instructions, and give the log instructions to the homeowner. Refit the glass door, centered and latched.

• Logs and coals must not block the pilot flame or the main burner flame.
  • Glass door: set the two bottom tabs in the firebox slots, centered left to right; rotate the door in until the gasket touches the firebox frame; hook both top spring latches with the glass latch tool, hooks facing down.
  • The glass gasket is a 4-piece assembly. Check that the pieces butt together at the corners; gaps cause exhaust leaks and acrid smells. Verify the glass frame is properly latched.
Test fire & set air shutters

Fresh remote batteries, remote synchronized. The pilot must light both burners immediately, and the flame must be stable, not lifting, after 5 minutes. After about 30 minutes' warm-up, fine-tune the air shutters and the vent damper by flame appearance.

• Burners light immediately and the flame runs promptly along the rear burner. Don't continue unless the burner cycles on/off without delays.
  • Flame still lifting after 5 minutes: turn off, check that every vent joint is twist-locked and leak-proof and the cap is right-side-up.
  • Shutter levers sit below the glass door frame: front burner on the left (slide left to open, right to close), rear burner on the right (right to close, left to open). Move them with the glass latch tool.
  • Flame too blue: close in 1/8" steps. Soot on the glass: open fully until it stops, burn four to six hours fully open, then close in 1/8" steps. Give each setting about ½ hr. Above 4,500', some variation may be needed.
  • LP: aim for a blue base about 2" high; yellow flame starting at the burner surface means open the shutter.
  • Vent damper (rod above the glass frame, center of the convection chamber): judge the flames after 20 minutes; never close it fully on a horizontal termination. Ghosting, or sooting on LP: open it fully and work back. Hook the rod with the glass latch tool, pull out about 1/8" and turn clockwise to close.
  • At maximum after 30 minutes or more, a normal rear flame is 1 to 2 inches above the top edge of the rear log.
Note: p. 68 gives the air shutter setting as 0" to ⅛" for natural gas and ¼" to fully open for LP; p. 69 gives ⅛" open for natural gas and ½" minimum for LP.
Cure & hand over

With the barrier screen and front installed, run the 3-step curing cycle before finishing materials go on. Then train the homeowner (remote, IPI/CPI, lockout reset, backup battery, master switch, manual gas shutoff) and complete the warranty registration.

1. Step 1: Manual (Off) mode, flame Hi, fan level 3, at least 2 hours; turn off and let it cool. The blowers keep curing smoke from staining the wall finish above.
  2. Step 2: Manual mode, flame Hi, fan off, until curing odors diminish (about 3 hours); leave it on.
  3. Step 3: fan to level 1; if new odors appear, keep running until they diminish.

More than 10 continuous hours on high isn't unusual. Finishing materials in the non-combustible zone can see around 350° F; use materials rated for it (adhesives, wall substrates, paints and polishes are common odor sources).

Hand-over (checklist on p. 88)

  • Leave the manual packet: manuals, remote, glass latch tool, backup battery system.
  • Show how to remove and refit the decorative front and the glass door; explain the barrier screen requirement.
  • Remote: CPI and IPI, flame level, fan, accent light, rear burner and the three thermostat modes.
  • Lockout reset, backup battery use in an outage, the master switch's emergency shutoff, the manual gas valve with the glass latch tool, and required periodic maintenance.

panels.title: Soot on the glass or logs
items: Burner air shutter closed too far → open it fully
Exhaust damper closed too far → open it
Glass door seal compromised → check the gasket; replace one that is white through the bulb with failed adhesive
Incorrect gas pressure or burner orifice size → check orifices and outlet pressure (3.5" W.C. NG; 10" W.C. LP)

panels.title: Pilot slow to light, or sparking won't stop
items: Pilot should light within five to eight seconds of sparking; over ten seconds → check spark rod position and igniter wires for pinched or damaged areas
Pilot lit but sparking continues after five seconds → dirty flame sensor: clean with emery cloth and retry
Still sparking → check the flame sensor lead wire for damage or grounding problems

panels.title: Delayed ignition, lifting or ghosting flames
items: Logs or coals blocking the pilot or main burner flame
Vent not leak-proof → every joint twist-locked, cap right-side-up
Pilot flame not reaching the burners → at least 1" long, overlapping the propagation ports on both burners
Slow flame propagation → remove debris, vacuum the burner ports and retry
Flames ghosting off the burners → open the vent damper fully, then work back in increments
"Low profile" vent caps → not approved: prone to exhaust recirculation and ghosting

panels.title: Frequent lockout
items: Always wait at least five minutes before relighting
Many possible causes → diagnose and find the primary cause; never assume the ignition control is faulty
Cold flue in winter → CPI keeps the flue warm, increases draft at start-up and aids in eliminating lockout

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace lights itself. An igniter sparks the pilot, and the pilot lights the burners. Never try to light the pilot by hand, and use only the supplied remote.

Before you light it

  • Smell all around the fireplace for gas, including next to the floor. Some gas is heavier than air and settles low. If you smell gas, stop and see “Gas smell & safety.”
  • Check that the master switch is on. It's at the bottom left corner of the fireplace, in the left-side air gap. The remote can't reach the fireplace unless it's on.
  • The barrier screen must be in place whenever the fireplace runs.

To light it

  1. Press ON/OFF on the remote.
  2. The fireplace beeps and the igniter sparks. Once the pilot is lit and steady, the gas valve opens and the burners light at full flame.
  3. Turn the flame down to a level you like with the remote.

In a thermostat mode it only lights if your set temperature is above the room temperature. To turn it off, press ON/OFF again.

If the pilot doesn't light, the system locks out. Press ON/OFF to turn it off, then wait five minutes for any gas to clear before you press ON/OFF again. If it still won't run, shut off its gas (see “Gas smell & safety”) and call your service technician or gas supplier.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The remote comes programmed to your fireplace and takes 3 AAA batteries. Use it within 20' of the fireplace. You'll hear a beep each time a button press is received. No beep? Press again.

The buttons

  • ON/OFF turns the fireplace on or off.
  • Thermostat picks the mode: OFF (Manual), ON (Normal) or SMART.
  • Mode steps through flame height, fan speed, accent light and rear burner.
  • Up / Down changes the setting shown, or the set temperature.

Thermostat modes

  • Manual: runs whatever the room temperature. It shuts itself off after 24 hours.
  • Normal: cycles on and off to hold your set temperature. The fan starts five minutes after start-up and stops 12-1/2 minutes after the flames go out.
  • Smart: holds the temperature by turning the flame up and down for you.

In Normal and Smart, the fireplace shuts off if it hears nothing from the remote for 60 minutes, for example if the remote is in another room or its batteries are weak.

Flame height and accent light have six levels each; the fan has six speeds and off. For less heat, turn off the rear burner and lower the flame.

Child lock: press MODE and UP together; do it again to unlock. °F / °C: turn the fireplace off, then press MODE and the thermostat button together.

Don't leave it burning unattended for long in Manual mode; the room can overheat. In a bedroom, study or other closed-off room, always use a thermostat mode.

curing.title: First fires: smoke and odor are normal
curing.html:
A new fireplace needs a heat cure. Materials left from manufacturing burn off and the paint hardens, so expect some smoke and odor at first. This is normal. Your installer should run the cure as the last install step, before finishing materials go on around the fireplace.

The 3-step cure

  1. With the barrier screen and front in place, turn it on in Manual (OFF) mode, flame on Hi, fan on level 3. Run it at least 2 hours, then turn it off and let it cool.
  2. Turn it on again in Manual mode, flame on Hi, fan off. Run it until the odors fade, about 3 hours, and leave it on.
  3. Set the fan to level 1. If new odors appear, keep it running until they fade.
Expect visible smoke and a strong odor in step 1. It will set off smoke alarms, so you may disable them first. Open doors and windows for fresh air. The fan keeps the smoke from staining the wall above.

More than 10 hours on high isn't unusual. Slight odors can return on later start-ups and fade with use.

Also normal

  • A burnt dust and lint smell the first time after three months or more unused, just like your furnace in the fall.
  • Small noises as the steel expands and contracts.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass now and then, and only once it has cooled to room temperature.

  • Outside: any glass cleaner you like.
  • Inside: Kel Kem Polish Plus (part # 65-06-00455) or a comparable product. Never oven cleaner or abrasive cleaners.

The additives that give gas its smell can leave a white film on the glass. It comes off if you clean it promptly.

Taking the glass door off

  1. Use the glass latch tool on the two spring latches at the top. Put it in the hole in each latch, pull toward you and turn it 180 degrees to unhook. Leave the hooks upside-down so the door goes back on easily.
  2. With both hands, tip the top of the frame out about 8", lift it 1" at an angle and move it away.
  3. To refit, set the two bottom tabs in their slots, centered. Tip the door in until the gasket touches, then hook the latches with the tool.

Check the gasket each time the door comes off. Never run the fireplace with the glass off, cracked or broken.

A black film is soot. Soot on the glass, soot patches bigger than 1"x1" on the logs, or soot outside around the vent cap: turn the fireplace off right away and tell your Mendota dealer.

modes.title: Pilot modes: IPI or CPI
modes.html:
The electronic ignition lights a pilot first, then the pilot lights the burners. You choose how the pilot behaves:

  • IPI (Intermittent Pilot Ignition): the pilot is off when the fireplace isn't running, and lights automatically when you turn it on.
  • CPI (continuous pilot): the pilot stays on, and shuts off after 7 days without use. Each use restarts the 7-day clock.

To switch modes

  1. With the remote off, press MODE. The screen shows CPI or IPI.
  2. Press UP for CPI or DOWN for IPI.
  3. Press ON/OFF to start the fireplace.

A snowflake icon shows on the screen the whole time you're in CPI.

Why CPI in winter

A lit pilot keeps the chimney warm for a good draft at start-up and helps prevent lockouts. It also stops excess condensation on the glass, and keeps the fireplace body warm against cold drafts and heat loss.

Note: p. 10 says CPI is required in winter when outside daily highs stay at 50°F or lower; p. 75 recommends it when the average daily high falls below 50°F.

Turning the flame down past level one shuts the burners off. In IPI the pilot goes out too; in CPI it stays lit.

wontstart.title: When it won't turn on
wontstart.html:
If the remote works but the fireplace won't start, or it only beeps back, it may be in lockout. That's the safety shutdown after the pilot fails to light.

Reset a lockout

  1. Turn the remote off.
  2. Turn it on and wait two seconds.
  3. Turn it off and wait two seconds.
  4. Turn it on and wait two seconds.
  5. Turn it off.

Then turn the remote on and start the fireplace. Always wait at least five minutes after a lockout before relighting.

Also check

  • The master switch is on (bottom left corner, in the left-side air gap).
  • The remote batteries. A battery icon appears on its screen when they're low.
  • No beep at all? Re-pair the remote. With the master switch on, press and release the sync button just above it; the fireplace beeps three times. Within seven seconds, press the remote's on button. Four beeps means it's paired.
If it still won't start, or lockouts keep happening, call your Mendota dealer. Frequent lockouts have many possible causes and need a proper diagnosis.

power.title: Power outages & batteries
power.html:
Your fireplace runs on house power. If the power goes out, it can still run on the battery pack that came with it.

  1. Get the battery pack and its connecting harness. Keep both in a safe and secure place for outages; your installer should show you how they work.
  2. Plug the pack into the fireplace's backup power inlet, the labeled cover plate mounted to the left of the fireplace.

On battery power, the burners and the flame height control work. The fan and accent light don't; they need house power.

Backup pack4 × AA (6V DC max.)
Remote3 × AAA

Change the remote batteries at least every 6 months, or more often with heavy use. A battery icon on the remote's screen means they're running low.

If a Versiheat or FlexHeat system was installed so a TV can hang above the fireplace, the fireplace can't be used during a power outage, because that system has to be running.

safety.title: Gas smell & safety
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions.
  • Can't reach them? Call the fire department.
Follow these steps exactly. If you don't, a fire or explosion may result, causing property damage, personal injury and loss of life.

To shut off the gas

  1. Press ON/OFF on the remote, and turn off CPI pilot mode.
  2. Close the shutoff valve inside the fireplace, in the left-side convection chamber. Put the tip of the glass latch tool in the arrow-shaped bracket and turn it down 90 degrees, until it stops.
  3. Also close the outside shutoff valve, if your installer fitted one.

In an emergency, switch the master switch off to stop the main burners.

Around the fireplace

  • The barrier screen must always be on when it runs. Keep furniture at least 60" in front of it, and nothing on the front edge of the mantel.
  • The glass and nearby surfaces get too hot to touch. That's normal, so supervise children and pets; a safety gate is recommended.
  • Never burn wood or paper in it. Don't use it if any part has been under water.

care.title: Upkeep & annual service
care.html:
Have a qualified installer, service agency or your gas supplier service the fireplace every year, in the summer or early fall. Any adjustment to the burner, pilot or logs is their job too.

The yearly service

  • Clean lint and dust around the controls and blowers, and check the wiring.
  • Clean the pilot's flame sensor and sparker rods, and check the pilot flames.
  • Vacuum the burner ports. Insects like to nest there, attracted by the odorant added to natural gas.
  • Clean the logs and coals and check them for carbon.
  • Check the glass door gasket and the vent cap, and clean the glass.

Your part

  • Look at the outside vent cap monthly. Leaves, twigs or other debris mustn't block it.
  • Change the remote batteries at least every 6 months.
  • Lint from carpet and bedding can mean more frequent cleaning.
  • See large soot patches or a black film on the glass? Turn it off and call your dealer.
The warranty makes you, the original purchaser, responsible for annual maintenance. Problems caused by a lack of maintenance can void it.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Mendota gives the original purchaser a limited lifetime warranty, as long as the fireplace stays where it was first installed. It can't be transferred. Coverage starts on the date Mendota invoices your installing dealer, and applies only to new units sold through an authorized Mendota dealer.

Which parts are covered, and for how long, is shown as a table on the manual's warranty page (linked below). Labor credits exclude travel and mileage; parts credits exclude freight.

Making a claim

Report the problem to your Mendota dealer within 30 days, with proof of purchase, the purchase date, the model name and the serial number. Those numbers are on the listing label, which pulls out from the air gap below the glass door frame.

Not covered

  • Discoloration and some minor warping. Both are normal.
  • Noises from the steel expanding and contracting.
  • Water damage, and odors from water or the environment.
  • Over-firing above the unit's listed BTU rating.
  • Plated surfaces damaged by cleaners other than denatured alcohol. Wipe off fingerprints before the first fire.
  • Removing or reinstalling hearths, facings or mantels.
Proper permits and inspections, and a dealer-approved installer, are needed for valid claims. This is a summary; the full terms are in the manual.

specInput.title: Input rates & orifices
specInput.html:
NG high / low fire45,500 / 13,450 BTUH
LP high / low fire45,500 / 15,840 BTUH
P.4 fireplace efficiency71.92%
Maker's website: CSA P.4.1 Efficiency 72%.
Orifices, 0–2000 ftrear #37 NG / 1/16" LP · front #44 NG / #55 LP

Ships configured for natural gas; LP needs conversion kit #HA-88-00080 (see the LP conversion step). Orifice sizes are stamped on the orifice body. Verify them and the input rate at installation.

Note: for the high-altitude orifices (2000–4500 ft), p. 15 gives rear #37 NG and front #56 LP; p. 46 gives rear #38 NG with front #55 LP ("for all elevations").

High altitude: check with the local gas supplier whether the gas is already derated before changing orifices. Above 7,500 ft, contact Mendota Technical Service. Never over-fire or under-fire by changing orifice sizes or gas pressure: over-firing can permanently damage the firebox, under-firing can cause delayed ignition, and both void the warranty.

specPressure.title: Gas pressures
specPressure.html:
NG supply7" W.C. (5.0" min., 11" max.)
LP supply11" W.C. (11" min., 13" max.)
NG manifold3.5" WC ± 1/8"
LP manifold10.0" WC ± 1/8"

Supply pressures are from the ratings page; the manifold settings come from the input-rate verification (p. 46). Two pressure taps on the main gas valve check inlet and outlet pressure. Correct pressure and proper line sizing are imperative; have the gas supplier or plumber check both.

Supply-piping pressure tests: above 1/2 psi (3.5 kPa), disconnect the appliance and its main gas valve; at 1/2 psi or less, isolate it by closing its shutoff valve.

If sooting continues after the shutter, damper and gasket checks, the troubleshooting chart has a service person check orifice sizes and outlet pressure (3.5" W.C. NG; 10" W.C. LP).

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Coaxial rigid pipe, 5" diameter exhaust and 8" diameter air inlet, with approved vent caps. All UL Listed coaxial rigid 5"X8" components and caps are approved, but don't mix brands or series. Twist-lock every joint (about ¼ turn clockwise). No silicone sealant at pipe joints; stove gasket cement may be used but isn't required. Use fixed lengths in place of telescoping sections whenever possible. No "low profile" vent caps. Each appliance gets its own vent; never connect to a chimney serving another appliance.

Master Venting Chart (V = first vertical off the collar)

V 12 in.H max 1'-6"
V 18 in.H max 4'-7"
V 24 in.H max 7'-8"
V 36 in.H max 13'-10"
V 4 ft – 30 ftH max 20'
V 31 ft – 50 ftH max 50' – V
  • 12" minimum vertical connected directly to the flue starter collar.
  • Zone A (first vertical under 4 ft): the chart already includes one 90° elbow; subtract 3 ft for each additional 90°.
  • Zone B (first vertical 4 to 30 ft): up to 20 ft horizontal and three 90° elbows anywhere, no reduction; four 90° elbows only with a vertical termination.
  • Two 45° elbows may replace one 90°; each horizontally positioned 45° takes 1½' off the maximum horizontal. One foot of 45° pipe equals 8-1/2" horizontal and 8-1/2" vertical.
  • All straight sections combined: 54 ft or less. Vertical: 50 ft maximum from the top of the fireplace.
  • Horizontal runs level or rising ¼" per foot toward the termination, never downward. Support every 3 ft.
Note: p. 57 gives the 18 in. row 4'-7" maximum horizontal; the same chart on p. 60 gives 4'-6".
Note: for the 36 in. row, the chart gives 13'-10" on pp. 57 and 60, but the worked example on p. 58 uses 13'-4" for a 3 ft starter (7'-4" with three 90° elbows).
Note: for four-elbow runs, pp. 57 and 58 allow four 90° elbows in Zone B (4 to 30 ft starter) with a vertical termination and no reduction from 20 ft, but the four-elbow table on p. 64 lists 12' maximum horizontal (H1+H2+H3) for a 4'- 30' starter, and its 3' / 5' / 9' for 12" / 2' / 3' starters don't follow its own rule of taking 6 feet off the Zone A chart.

Above 7,500 ft, contact Mendota technical service for venting requirements. A Mendota-approved power vent is an alternative; follow its own instructions.

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Unit to floor0"
Unit to enclosure side walls / back wall1/2"
Unit bottom to enclosure ceiling55"
Unit bottom to room ceiling72"
Glass frame edge to adjacent side wall16"
Vent pipe top / sides / bottom3" / 1" / 1"

Combustible side walls, mantel legs, corbels and decorative objects must sit behind a 45° line from the side edges of the visible glass unless they're more than 16" away. A wall at 45° to the glass starting at the fireplace's outer edge is permitted.

Can't meet 16" to an existing combustible wall? NFPA 211 reductions: a 20-gauge or heavier steel shield on at least 1" metal or ceramic standoffs (1" active airspace, top and bottom left open, at least 12" larger than the heat source in each direction) cuts it by 66%, to 5-3/8"; an R-1 rated ceramic or mineral board cuts it by 50%, to 8".

Note: the manual measures the 16" side-wall clearance from the glass frame edge on p. 15, from the side edges of the facing guide on p. 17, and from the side edge of the visible glass on p. 22.

Never fill vent air spaces with insulation, and don't let trim or surrounds seal the convection air openings. In a cavity deeper than 22-1/2", all framing and finishing protruding past the fireplace front must be non-combustible. Mantels: see the mantel card.

specMantel.title: Combustible mantels & TVs
specMantel.html:
Measure from the fireplace's floor level, or from the top of the convection air opening (the usual reference).

8" mantel54" above floor level
Top of convection air opening35" above floor level

For mantels that protrude more than 8", use a 3:4 rise and run. The manual's example: a 12" mantel sits 12" x (3/4) + 13" = 22" above the convection air opening. Shallower mantels, and the area where only non-combustible facing is allowed, follow the mantel chart drawn on this page.

Note: p. 23 gives the top of the convection air opening as 35" above floor level in its text, and 34-7/8" from floor level to the top air gap in a note on the same page.

TV above the fireplace

  • Mantel at least 2" deeper than the TV and at least as wide, its top surface at least 12" above the top air gap. If the mantel is combustible, make certain the entire mantel meets the combustible mantel clearance requirements.
  • Or a recessed cavity at least 6" taller and 6" wider than the TV, its bottom at least 16" above the top air gap, with the TV recessed at least 2".
  • Or a heat transfer system (Cool Wall, two Versiheat fans, or FlexHeat) for a TV 12" above the top air gap. The convection fans must be off; Versiheat or FlexHeat must run whenever the fireplace does.

Installing a TV there is the homeowner's decision; Mendota isn't liable for effects on the TV.

specFraming.title: Rough framing & chase
specFraming.html:
Enclosure width51"
Finished framing width45"
Height48 1/2"
Depth22-1/2"
Vent opening (H x W)10-3/4" x 10-3/4"
Net weight325 lbs (team lift)

Keep the 51" enclosure width so the unit can be centered; once it's in, the front can be framed to 45". The ignition-system box protrudes from the left side; its front face is 3-5/8" in from the unit's front face.

Set the unit on a wood, masonry or metal surface extending its full width and depth, never directly on carpet, vinyl or other combustibles. On a cement slab, plywood underneath helps stop cold conducting up. Build the chase like an outside wall: insulated, with vapor and air barriers, fire stops and gas-line holes sealed with high-temperature caulk. Mobile homes (USA): bolt the unit to the floor and ground it.

Note: pp. 15, 17 and 20 give the minimum depth as 22-1/2"; the side-wall clearance drawing on p. 22 is labeled 19-1/2" min. depth.

specHearth.title: Hearth pad
specHearth.html:
Hearth protectornon-combustible, R-1
Depth in front18" min.
Raised off the floor2" less depth per 1"
Raised 6" or moreno R-1 pad required

No R-1 rating is needed under the fireplace; it can sit on a wood or cement floor. Raising it only removes the pad requirement: the floor in front can still reach 200 °F, and a pad's top surface as high as 250°F. With carpet, vinyl or laminate in front, Mendota recommends raising the fireplace at least 12".

Thickness: p. 12 gives the R-1 pad a 1-1/2" maximum. The standard bottom finishing guide sits 1 1/2" ("A") above the bottom of the fireplace, and that gap must be covered: build the pad level with the guide, or raise the fireplace and cover the gap with non-combustible wall finish. A pad thicker than "A" means raising the fireplace by the difference (4" pad: raise 2 1/2"). Other guide kits can change "A".

Stone has a low R-value (1" granite: 0.05), so an insulating underlayment under non-combustible finish may be needed: Rescor 360 ceramic board 1/2" (R 1.11), Fiberfrax Duraboard LD 1/2" (R 1.10), or Micore 160, 300, SB mineral fiber board 1/2".

Note: p. 24 gives 1/2" Micore 160, 300, SB an R-value of 1.27 – 1.47; the same table on p. 26 gives 1.2 – 1.4.

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
AC supply120 VAC, hot at all times, no switch
Minimum line voltage110 Volts AC
Current1.5 Amps (p. 15) · 2 Amp (p. 39)
Backup6V DC power source
Note: p. 15 gives the current rating as 120 Volts AC, 1.5 Amps; p. 39 gives 120 VAC, 2 Amp.

Connect at the junction box on the left-side access box: remove its cover plate (two screws), route the house cable through the strain relief, and join the color-coded wires with the supplied wire nuts (braided to braided: strip both at least ½" and twist; braided to solid: strip the solid ½" and the braided ¾", and twist the braid around the solid). Close the box and plug in the house-power plug (labeled TO HOUSE POWER, in the manual packet); the plugs can't go in the wrong place. Ground per local codes, or NFPA 70 / CSA C22.1.

DC backup inlet: install the supplied harness, single-gang box and cover plate on the left side. The 6-foot harness lets the box sit up to 5 feet to the left; box center at 18" maximum height, or match the room's other outlets. Don't staple the harness to the studs. White and beige cover plates are supplied; attach the decal once the installation is verified, and show the homeowner how to connect the backup pack.

Label all wires before disconnecting during service; replacement wires must have the same type and size of insulation.

index_extra.p: What to do if you smell gas
Reset sequence; wait five minutes before relighting
IPI or CPI; CPI keeps the pilot on for up to 7 days
Black film or large soot patches: turn it off, call your dealer
Smoke from the first curing step sets them off
Mantel, recessed cavity or heat transfer kit

conflicts.issue: Current rating: 'ELECTRICAL REQUIREMENTS: 120 Volts AC, 1.5 Amps' (ratings information) vs '120 VAC, 2 Amp power or a 6V DC power source' (3.3 Electrical).

High-altitude (2000-4500 ft) orifices: ratings page lists rear #37 NG / 1/16" LP and front #44 NG / #56 LP; Gas Input Rate Verification says NG #38 rear / #44 front for all elevations above 2000 ft, LP 1/16" rear / #55 front for all elevations, and #38/#44 NG, 1/16"/#55 LP for 610-1370 m. Also shown in step5.
Master Venting Chart, 18 in. vertical: H max 4'-7" on p. 57 vs 4'-6" in the same chart on p. 60.
36 in. (3 ft) vertical: the chart gives 13'-10" (pp. 57, 60) but Example 1 on p. 58 says a 3 ft starter allows 13'-4" 'per Master Venting Chart' and derives 7'-4" with three 90° elbows.

Four 90° elbows: chart note 7 (p. 57) and 'Using 90° Elbows in Zone B' (p. 58) allow four 90° elbows with vertical termination and no reduction from the 20 ft maximum horizontal when the first vertical is 4-30 ft; the four-elbow table (p. 64) gives H1+H2+H3 = 12' (V2 max 26') for V1 4'-30', and 3'/5'/9' for V1 12"/2'/3', which also don't follow p. 64's prerequisite #3 (subtract 6 ft from the Zone A chart maximum). Its V2 max 50' with a 12" V1 also exceeds the 50 ft maximum vertical.

Ceiling fire-stop framing: 10 ½" x 10 ½" opening for the mandatory ceiling fire stop (p. 60 step 3, p. 62 step 2) vs fire stops at the second floor and above 'framed to 10" x 10" inside dimensions as described in step No. 4' (p. 62; step 4 is the 10" x 10" roof opening).

Reference point for the 16" side-wall clearance: 'glass frame edge to adjacent sidewall' (ratings, p. 15); 'side edges of the facing guide' (p. 17, repeated in the p. 22 figure); 'side edge of the visible glass' (p. 22 text).
Minimum framing depth 22-1/2" (pp. 15, 17, 20) vs Figure 3-7 (Side Wall Clearances, p. 22) labeled '19-1/2" MIN. DEPTH'. The same figure shows 9" to vent pipe center where p. 17 shows 9-3/8".
Top of the convection air opening: '35 inches up from the floor level' (p. 23 text) vs 'distance from the Floor Level of this Fireplace to the Top Air Gap is 34-7/8"' (p. 23 figure note).
R-value of 1/2" Micore 160, 300, SB mineral fiber board: 1.27 – 1.47 (R-Values of Hearth Pad Boards, p. 24) vs 1.2 – 1.4 (same table repeated, p. 26).
Air shutter opening: lighting checklist '0" to ⅛" for natural gas or ¼" to fully open for LP gas' (p. 68) vs '1/8" open for natural gas and 1/2" minimum open for L.P. gas' (4.12, p. 69).

CPI in winter: 'It is required to activate the Continuous Pilot Mode (CPI) ... during winter months when outside daily high temperatures remain 50oF or lower' (p. 10) vs 'Mendota recommends that CPI mode is used during the winter months when the average daily high temperature falls below 50°F' (p. 75).

Finish depth for the Grace/Willowbrook/Mission guide kits: 'When the wall finish material will exceed 2 ½" in depth, the Recessed Mount guide kit will be required' vs the Flush Mount kit 'requires that your finish material be less than 3" thick including backing materials'.

review.notes: One manual (85-03-01108-X, 94 pp.). The title's 'Traditional' is the catalog name; the manual calls the unit 'FV46 Fullview Direct Vent Gas Fireplace Heater', model no. AA-11-03763. Catalog checks that match the manual: BTU inputs 45,500/13,450 NG and 45,500/15,840 LP, 5 x 8 vent, 325 lb, standard dual blowers (190 CFM, p. 19), US manufactured-home approval, IPI ignition, ANSI Z21.88/CSA 2.33. Efficiency: manual 'P.4 fireplace efficiency 71.92%' (p. 15) vs website 'CSA P.4.1 Efficiency 72%': shown as a website note in specInput and listed in catalog_mismatches. Catalog height/width/depth (48.5/45/22.5) equal the manual's minimum rough-framing dimensions; the unit's own outside dimensions appear only in the p. 17 drawing, so they weren't compared. The catalog's view area (38" x 33 5/16") isn't in the manual. Ignition: the PF2 IPI system also has a selectable CPI mode (p. 75); the catalog says 'IPI', consistent with the ratings text. Figure-only or image content not transcribed: warranty coverage table (p. 89, image only, so the warranty drawer points to it); mantel profile chart (p. 23); dimension drawings (pp. 17, 20, 21, 22); approved vent configurations (p. 36); the unlabeled vent tables on pp. 61 and 63 (their 36 in. values 10'-4" and 7'-4" follow the p. 58 example's 13'-4", while their 24 in. 3'-8" doesn't follow the chart's 7'-8" less 3 ft); power-vent configuration diagrams (pp. 66-67); LP regulator figure label [10.0-5.5"WC] (p. 51). The gas-line sizing table (p. 43) has garbled column headers, so the guide points to it instead of transcribing. Pages 13, 14, 18, 21, 40 and 67 are mostly figures; p. 93 is blank. Minor differences kept out of the drawers: fan run-on 12-1/2 minutes (p. 72) vs '12 minutes' in the hand-over checklist (p. 88), guide uses p. 72; 'the AUX On function is not used in this fireplace' (p. 73) vs an Auxiliary function for optional heat transfer kits (p. 74), AUX not covered; furniture 60" from the barrier screen (pp. 2, 16) vs from the fireplace front (p. 8); 110VAC (p. 78) vs 120 VAC (pp. 15, 39); CPI is called 'Continuous Pilot Mode' (p. 10) and 'Pilot on Demand' (p. 75), guide says continuous pilot; two lockout resets (p. 76: ON/OFF off, wait five minutes, ON/OFF; p. 80: off/on cycle with two-second waits), both used; the accent light ships installed (p. 50) though the p. 47 checklist says to install it; p. 76 says the door must remain on during pilot ignition 'except for the First Time Lighting', exception unexplained, not carried in; hearth pad '1-1/2" Thick Maximum' (p. 12) alongside p. 25's raise-the-fireplace example for a 4" pad, both shown in specHearth. Pilot location is described as 'right side of firebox where the rear and front burner ends meet' (p. 53) and 'in the center of the firebox between the burners' (p. 83); the guide only uses the p. 53 wording in the LP conversion step. Metric slip: unit bottom to enclosure ceiling 55 in. printed as 127 cm (p. 15). No LED/blink-code table in the manual, so codes is empty; the beep signals (one beep per command, three beeps ready to sync, four beeps paired, beeping only = possible lockout) are in the owner drawers. Massachusetts requirements (licensed plumber or gas fitter, CO detector in the room, sidewall-vent rules; pp. 6, 9) are not carried into the guide.
